text.p: Olympiakos arrived for European basketball's annual showpiece, the Final Four championship, without the services of forward Evric Gray who has been suspended for three months after testing positive for ephedrine.
Gray tested positive for the banned substance after the Greek club's quarter-final against ex-champions Panathinaikos earlier this month and was suspended by FIBA, the international federation.

Gray replaced American compatriot Willie Anderson last December as Olympiakos struggled in the initial Euro League stages. But since the turn of the year they have moved up the gears and reached the Final Four with astonishing ease, deposing big Greek rivals Panathinaikos on the way.

Their opponents in Tuesday's first semifinal are Ljubljana of Slovenia, where basketball has taken off in recent seasons -- a fact underlined by the presence of nearly 100 media personnel from the more than 650 assembling at Rome's Palaeur stadium.
The championship, the 10th in its present format, will be seen on television in 150 countries worldwide, including the United States.

The biggest number of supporters will again be from Greece with Olympiakos expecting about 5,000 of their fans in the 10,000 capacity arena. Around 600 security personnel will be on hand to deal with any trouble.

Olympiakos have been a powerhouse in European basketball over the past few years, only to disappoint in previous Final Fours, worst of all in 1995 when they lost in the final for the second year in succession.
They are injury-free for virtually the first time this season. Coach Dusan Ivkovic said: "We've not been lucky through the season so now I'm very pleased to have all my players at my disposal."
Club captain George Sigalas said: "It's important that we are all right for the first time and I hope we can offer the fans joy because they deserve it."
Tuesday's second semifinal is between last year's beaten finalists Barcelona and Villeurbanne of France, with the Spanish club favourites to reach Thursday's final.
